subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and if so should the first scope include warnings only, warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint, or full bounded deferral?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request defines new public config, session-state, and security semantics that determine whether agents get extra write/tool opportunity and whether compaction can be delayed under context pressure.

options.title: Adopt Warning And Handoff First
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in pre-threshold warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt Full Bounded Deferral
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with explicit max duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, workspace scope, and approval-expiry rules.

options.title: Decline New Lifecycle Surface
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoints as the supported compaction surfaces and route remaining needs to docs or plugins.

recommendation.title: Adopt Warning And Handoff First
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in pre-threshold warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for pre-compaction memory flush and the current config/runtime surface points to steipete.
